data.title: European shares slip as banks drag, oil-driven inflation fears weigh
data.description:
Key points:
  • STOXX 600 falls to three-week low, down 0.8%
  • Banks lead declines, UBS bottoms STOXX 600
  • US Fed decision awaited on Wednesday

By Sudeshna Ghoshal

European shares hit three-month lows on Tuesday, with banks leading losses, as surging oil prices and bond yields sapped risk appetite ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve's interest rate decision this week.

The pan-European STOXX 600 was down 0.8% at 630.99 points by 0840 GMT, its lowest since June 12. Most major regional bourses also traded lower.

Banks (.SX7P) and financial services stocks (.SXFP) were among the biggest drags, down 1.3% and 2.7%, respectively. Switzerland's largest bank UBS fell 4.2%, the biggest decliner among European stocks, while Deutsche Bank dipped 1.2%, UniCredit fell 2.3% and Standard Chartered slipped 2.1%.

Most sectors on the STOXX 600 were down in early trading.

Banking stocks took a hit a day after Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan warned that the U.S. lender's investment banking fees could drop by at least 10% in the third quarter, and that it expects sales and trading revenue to be nearly flat.

"The warning triggered worries that the bank could not carry on with strong earnings, which in turn helped readjust the earnings outlook to the downside," said Ipek Ozkardeskaya, senior analyst at Swissquote Bank.

"That's a big fear that the bank earnings may not be as strong as they have been in the last quarter... and that is pulling the valuation (and) the earnings outlook lower."

In a double whammy for markets, rising bond yields are further weighing on risk appetite. The benchmark U.S. 10-year Treasury yield breached 5% on Monday and topped its highest levels in nearly two decades.

As attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure continue, oil prices rose over 3% on Tuesday, reinforcing inflation concerns and prompting markets to increasingly price in rate hikes. The European Central Bank raised interest rates for the second time last week.

Markets are now squarely focused on the Fed's decision on Wednesday, where traders are pricing in an over 90% chance of a rate hike, according to LSEG data.

Separately, data showed Britain's job vacancies fell to a four-year low ahead of the Bank of England's rate decision on Thursday, when it is expected to hold rates steady.

Among individual stocks, Deutz slipped 4.5% after the firm offered up to 10% of its shares in a capital raise.

Evonik Industries shed 3% after Morgan Stanley downgraded its rating on the stock.

Puig shed 3% after the Spanish beauty group said on Monday it would take full control of ISDIN in a €1.20 billion ($1.41 billion) deal.

data.title: ZAWYA: Sasakawa Africa Association supports FCAIB with solar-powered irrigation system to boost cassava production
data.description:
By Staff Writer

The Federal College of Agriculture, Moor Plantation, Ibadan (FCAIB), has received from the Sasakawa Africa Association a solar-powered irrigation system, at the institution’s cassava agroforestry learning site.

The visit is part of the ongoing SIFTAS Project, a cassava agroforestry initiative funded by GIZ AgSys, implemented at the college to strengthen practical agricultural activities, research and the demonstration of sustainable farming practices.

Speaking during the visit, the Sasakawa Africa Association vendor, Engineer Mustapha Tajudeen, disclosed that the team was at the college to supply and install the solar-powered irrigation system for a one-acre agroforestry test plot.

The equipment supplied included three 650-watts solar panels, a hose and a pumping machine. The irrigation system is expected to provide a reliable water supply for the demonstration site, support agricultural activities beyond the rainy season and promote year-round farming and practical learning.

In his remarks, the provost of the college expressed appreciation to the Sasakawa Africa Association and GIZ AgSys for selecting FCAIB as one of the institutions to host the cassava agroforestry project. He also commended members of staff, whose efforts have contributed to attracting research projects, grants and development initiatives to the College.

The provost specifically acknowledged and applauded the Dean of of School of Agricultural Management and Vocational Studies, Dr. Adebayo Adeniran, for his contributions to promoting research activities and creating opportunities for the college through collaborations with development organisations.

He assured the visiting team of the institution’s commitment to the proper management and protection of the equipment provided for the project. He also directed relevant officials to work with the vendor to identify a suitable and secure location for the installation.

The provost stressed the importance of commencing the project promptly, noting that the irrigation system would facilitate agricultural activities throughout the year, including periods when students are on vacation.

He expressed gratitude to the Sasakawa Africa Association and the funding organizations – GIZ AgSys for their continued support, and assured them that the College would continue to uphold the confidence reposed in the institution.

The Registrar, Mrs. Olanike Popoola; Head of Bursary, Mr. Adeyemi Jaguno; Head of Library, Mrs. M. Osunkoya; Dean, School of Engineering, Atere Ayoade, Director of Audit, Mr. ‘Kunle Karunwi and other members of staff were also present during the visit.

The visit concluded with arrangements for the installation of the solar-powered irrigation system at the designated cassava agroforestry learning site.

data.title: ZAWYA: Yadea partners with Spiro in push to electrify Africa’s two-wheelers
data.description:
By Staff Writer

Chinese electric two-wheeler manufacturer Yadea has partnered with African electric mobility company Spiro to expand electric transport across the continent.

The partnership will see Yadea supply electric two-wheelers and related products for Spiro's markets, while Spiro integrates the vehicles into its battery-swapping and energy infrastructure.

The companies also plan to develop two-wheeler platforms adapted to local road conditions and commercial use in African markets.

The agreement was announced in Dubai on 11 September and brings together Yadea's manufacturing and product development capabilities with Spiro's operating network and battery-swapping infrastructure, which spans seven African countries.

Focus on commercial mobility

The partnership is aimed in particular at commercial fleet operators, delivery services, logistics businesses and commuters using two-wheelers for daily transport.

Spiro will use Yadea's vehicles within its existing electric mobility ecosystem, including its battery-swapping network. The companies say the arrangement is intended to support the expansion of electric two-wheelers without relying solely on conventional charging infrastructure.

The two companies will also work on customised vehicle platforms for African conditions, although the announcement does not provide details on the models, specifications or markets that will receive them.

China-Africa electric mobility link

The deal strengthens the relationship between Chinese electric vehicle manufacturing and Africa's developing electric mobility market.

Yadea, which was founded in China, says it has sold more than 100 million electric two-wheelers across more than 100 countries and operates 10 production facilities globally. It also says it has more than 2,000 patents related to electric vehicle technology.

Spiro operates an electric mobility network across seven African countries, with battery swapping forming part of its infrastructure model.

Gagan Gupta, founder of Spiro and chairman of Equitane, said the partnership would allow the companies to combine Yadea's manufacturing scale with Spiro's understanding of African markets.

Anant Badjatya, CEO of Spiro, said the agreement would help the company respond to growing demand for electric mobility by increasing access to electric two-wheelers.

Wang Jiazhong, senior vice-president of Yadea Technology Group, said Africa represented an important market for zero-emission transport and that the partnership would combine Yadea's technology with Spiro's local infrastructure.

The announcement does not specify a timeline for the rollout of the new vehicles or identify which African markets will receive the first products.

data.title: ZAWYA: South Africa: FlySafair launches Johannesburg-Lusaka route
data.description:
By Staff Writer

FlySafair has launched a new route between Johannesburg and Lusaka, with five weekly flights connecting OR Tambo International Airport with Kenneth Kaunda International Airport.

The service operates on Mondays, Wednesdays, Thursdays, Fridays and Sundays, with the airline citing sustained demand on the Johannesburg-Lusaka corridor.

The Johannesburg-Lusaka service departs OR Tambo at 7.50am and arrives in Lusaka at 9.50am. The return flight leaves Kenneth Kaunda International Airport at 10.50am and arrives in Johannesburg at 12.50pm.

“Zambia has long been on our radar, and Lusaka is a route our customers have been asking about,” said Kirby Gordon, chief marketing officer at FlySafair.

“The Johannesburg–Lusaka corridor carries a significant mix of business and leisure travellers, as well as South Africans and Zambians travelling to see family and friends. We’re proud to bring our fares and our reliability to this route and to make the connection between our two countries more accessible than it has been.”

Route supports regional connectivity

The new service connects South Africa with Zambia’s capital, which serves as an important commercial centre for Southern and Central Africa.

Lusaka is home to regional banks, mining and telecommunications companies and pan-African development organisations, while South Africa remains one of Zambia’s significant trade and investment partners.

The route also provides access to tourism destinations beyond Lusaka, including Livingstone and Victoria Falls, the Lower Zambezi and South Luangwa national parks.

“Our international network has been built on the principle that connecting South Africa with its neighbours should be affordable, not a luxury,” added Gordon.

“When we launched Cape Town to Windhoek, we brought fares down significantly on that corridor, and we intend to do the same on Johannesburg to Lusaka. Zambia and South Africa have deep ties, and we’re glad to make staying connected a little easier.”

Source: FlySafair launches Johannesburg-Lusaka route

data.title: UK's Trustpilot shares slump as unchanged outlook disappoints investors
data.description:
By Atharva Singh

British online reviews platform Trustpilot's shares plummeted as much as 20% on Tuesday after the company left its earnings outlook unchanged, disappointing investors, despite strong AI-led revenues.

Here are details from the company's earnings report:

  • The company maintained its full-year forecast for high-teens constant-currency revenue growth and adjusted EBITDA margin improvement of two-to-three percentage points.

  • Adjusted core profit rose 46% to $26.3 million in the six months ended June 30, below a company-compiled estimate of $27 million.

  • Trustpilot's shares had gained about 60% through Monday's close, suggesting investors had been expecting a guidance upgrade as the company's AI initiatives and strong U.S. growth fueled optimism.

  • "This shows you the market wants upgrades from Trustpilot, not confirmations," said Angeline Ong, analyst at trading platform IG.

  • Trustpilot's revenue rose 23% to $151.4 million in the first half, and bookings rose 22%, both slightly ahead of expectations.

  • The platform reported a statutory net loss of $1.1 million, driven by one-off charges including an Italian antitrust fine and a provision for historical U.S. sales taxes.

  • J.P. Morgan analysts said the results were "noisier than usual", with a core profit miss, several one-off charges and the absence of a guidance upgrade.

  • Trustpilot was down 14.2% at 224.2p per share as of 9:30 AM GMT

data.title: US-based GE Vernova, Thailand's B.Grimm Power sign deals for gas turbine supply
data.description:
By Chayut Setboonsarng

U.S.-based energy technology company GE Vernova and Thailand's B.Grimm Power have signed two agreements to partner on power generation and energy infrastructure in Southeast Asia, the companies said on Tuesday.

Under the first agreement, GE Vernova will supply a gas turbine and associated generator for a gas-fired power plant project in Malaysia, owned and developed by B.Grimm Power, GE Vernova said in a statement.

Harald Link, chairman of B.Grimm Power, told reporters on the sidelines of the Gastech conference that the turbines will be delivered next year.

The power plant will be located in the Malaysian state of Perlis and will reach its commercial operating date in the fourth quarter of 2029, he added.

When asked about Malaysia's power market potential, Link said: "Every country gets a lot of data centers. That's why many countries invest in power generation and lines that connect to the grid."

Separately, GE Vernova and B.Grimm Power also entered a 14-year services agreement that covers five LM6000 gas turbine packages at B.Grimm Power's Bangkadi 1 and 2 power plants in Thailand for long-term operations.

The signing of the agreements took place at the Gastech exhibition and conference in Bangkok on Tuesday.

data.title: WTO says global trade system at critical juncture, urges reform
data.description:
Key points:
  • WTO urges reform as trade rules struggle with new economic realities
  • Fragmentation could cut global GDP by up to 6.9%
  • Poorer countries face biggest losses in breakdown scenarios
  • Regional trade blocs risk undermining multilateral cooperation without WTO rules

By Olivia Le Poidevin

The World Trade Organization on Tuesday urged its members to reform global trade rules or risk a slide into fragmentation that could significantly reduce economic output and hit poorer countries hardest.

In its annual report, the Geneva-based global trade body said existing rules have struggled to keep pace with shifts in economic power, the rise of industrial policy, digital trade and escalating political tensions between major powers.

The warning comes after the WTO's 166 members failed to reach agreement on a reform package at a ministerial meeting in Yaounde, Cameroon, in March, before relaunching talks in Geneva on issues including decision-making, dispute settlement and the challenges posed by subsidies and state intervention.

The WTO has struggled to find agreement on reforms among all members in the consensus-based organisation - as members are at different stages of economic development and with often conflicting interests.

WTO economists modelled a scenario in which the world fragments into competing geopolitical blocs and found global GDP would be 5.1% lower and exports 18.6% lower by 2050 than otherwise. In a more severe scenario, in which multilateral cooperation collapses and is replaced by a patchwork of free trade agreements, global GDP would fall 6.9% and exports nearly 27%.

By contrast, enhanced multilateral cooperation could raise global GDP by 2.9% and boost exports by almost 18%, according to the report. Least-developed countries would stand to gain the most from stronger cooperation, but could also suffer the largest losses from fragmentation.

TRADE AT A CROSSROADS

WTO Chief Economist Rob Staiger told Reuters the trading system was at a "critical juncture", citing four major challenges identified in the report: a broader distribution of economic power, growing state intervention in economies, changes in the nature of trade driven by digitalization and global value chains, and rising political friction.

"The rules are under strain and they really are having an impact. And if things fell apart at the global multilateral level, our scenarios are saying these would be the costs, and those costs would be quite large," Staiger said.

The findings come as countries increasingly pursue regional and sector-specific trade arrangements amid rising trade tensions and sweeping U.S. tariffs.

In March, a group of WTO members agreed to move ahead with the organisation's first baseline digital trade rules through a plurilateral agreement, bypassing opposition from some members.

Staiger said regional trade agreements and plurilateral initiatives could strengthen the multilateral system, but warned they could also undermine it if they evolved into competing blocs.

Without a strong WTO framework, such arrangements risk diverting trade towards preferred partners rather than the most efficient producers and encouraging blocs to raise barriers against outsiders, Staiger said. WTO rules help limit discrimination against non-members and constrain how free trade agreements are structured, he added.

The WTO said trade policy uncertainty had reached unprecedented levels in recent years as governments increasingly deploy tariffs, subsidies, export controls and industrial policies.

Although about 72% of global merchandise trade still takes place under WTO most-favoured-nation tariff terms, down from roughly 80% in 2022, Staiger called the decline a "worrisome trend" that underscored the risk of a gradual erosion of the multilateral trading system.

data.title: Global Trading System Facing Fragmentation or Revamp at 'Critical Juncture,' WTO Says
data.description:
By Paul Hannon

The splintering of the world trade system into a small number of geopolitical blocs or a larger number of regional groupings would lead to a significant reduction in economic activity by the middle of this century, the World Trade Organization said Tuesday.

The U.S. last year sharply raised tariffs on imports from around the world, and has continued to impose new duties on some countries. However, those moves have yet to provoke widespread retaliation, nor have other countries yet raised their tariffs on non-U.S. imports.

In an annual report, the Geneva-based dispute resolution body estimates that 72% of world trade in goods is still taking place on terms compatible with its non-discriminatory rules, down from 80%. Despite the higher tariffs and heightened uncertainty about policy, trade flows grew rapidly in 2025 and the first half of this year, boosted by the AI investment boom.

However, economists at the WTO don't believe the status quo can be sustained, and instead called for a concerted effort to repair and refresh the multilateral trade system.

"There are underlying tensions that do need to be addressed, and if left unaddressed, will continue to roil the world trading system," said Robert Staiger, the WTO's chief economist. "Most members agree that the status quo is not really an option. So either successful reform will occur or the status quo will not be the outcome."

The WTO examined two ways in which the trading system might fragment. In one scenario, many countries would trade relatively freely within geopolitical blocs likely centered on the U.S. and China, but commerce between those blocs would be limited. The trade body's economists estimate that would lower global exports by 18.6% and economic output 5.1% in 2050.

An alternative path would see flows of exports and imports centered on free trade agreements, which have proliferated in recent years. In that scenario, exports would be 26.9% lower and gross domestic product down 6.9%, with the poorest countries suffering the largest losses.

By contrast, the WTO said a reshaped system of "enhanced cooperation" in which most goods were traded among an expanded number of countries at lower tariffs would raise world exports by 17.9% and GDP by 2.9% in 2050.

"The cost of inaction on reform would be up to 10% of global GDP," said Staiger. "The world trading system really is at a critical juncture."

The WTO's economists have identified a number of reasons for the tensions that now surround world trade. For one, the period of freer trade that accompanied the creation of the WTO in 1995 has profoundly changed the world economy, and in particular raised the relative importance of China and other developing economies.

Deals that seemed to make sense for all parties then have aged badly for richer economies such as the U.S. Under WTO rules developing economies are entitled to preferential treatment that was intended to give them the time and flexibility to adjust to freer trade with more advanced countries.

The WTO said that while some developing economies should still receive preferential treatment, others are now "globally competitive economies with significant market power."

While freer trade helped spur rapid growth in many economies, the WTO said it has not lifted the poorest countries, and it has disadvantaged factory workers in rich countries that were most exposed to low-wage competition.

At the same time, international rivalries and suspicions have grown more intense, and governments now place a greater stress on national security in deciding trade policy.

"Economic power is more widely distributed, production is more interconnected, and domestic policies generate larger cross-border spillovers," Staiger said. "And those changes now interact with intensifying geopolitical rivalry."

The ways in which governments intervene in economies have also become more varied and widespread, with China and others pursuing industrial policies that many of their trading partners regard as unfair subsidies to already competitive businesses.

The WTO didn't offer a blueprint for reshaping the world trade system to reduce tensions and prevent fragmentation, leaving those questions to its members.

data.title: Aixia receives strategically important SEK 9 million data protection order for AI environment
data.description:
White Pearl Technology Group AB (publ) ("WPTG" or the "Group") announces that Aixia Group AB (publ) ("Aixia") has secured a strategically important order from an existing Swedish customer operating within AI and the automotive industry. The order relates to a significant expansion of the customer's data protection platform and has an initial order value of approximately SEK 9 million. The full announcement from Aixia follows below.

Aixia has received a strategically important order from an existing Swedish customer operating within AI and the automotive industry. The order covers a significant expansion of the customer's existing data protection platform and has an initial valueof approximately SEK 9 million.

The customer develops advanced AI-based solutions and manages very large volumes of valuable data that form a critical part of its development activities. The investment expands the capacity for secure data protection, backup and recovery to support continued data growth and increasingly demanding requirements for availability and resilience.

The solution is based on a modern, scalable data protection architecture designed for large and rapidly growing data volumes. The platform enables centralized data protection, automated backup and rapid recovery in the event of technical failures, operational incidents or cyberattacks.

"Data is one of the most important assets for companies developing advanced AI solutions. As data volumes continue to grow, so do the requirements for how that data is protected, stored and recovered. This investment is therefore strategically important for the customer, and we are very proud of the continued trust placed in Aixia to develop such a critical part of their AI infrastructure," says Mattias Bergkvist, CEO of Aixia.

The order further strengthens Aixia's position within AI infrastructure and data protection and demonstrates the breadth of the company's offering, spanning compute infrastructure and storage to security, data protection and the operation of business-critical environments.

data.title: ZAWYA: Singularity Summit South Africa 2026 unveils full programme
data.description:
AI, leadership, investment and digital transformation among the business opportunities set to drive two days of discussion in Johannesburg.

As artificial intelligence and exponential technologies are quietly reshaping industries, business models and the global economy, organisations face a growing challenge: deciding where the real opportunities lie and how quickly to act on them.

These questions will be at the heart of Singularity Summit South Africa 2026, which has unveiled its full programme ahead of the Summit at the Sandton Convention Centre in Johannesburg on Wednesday 21 and Thursday 22 October. Presented in collaboration with Old Mutual, event sponsors Google Cloud and Industrial Development Corporation (IDC), and metaverse partner UBU, this year’s Summit will bring together over 40 speakers from around the world to examine the technologies, ideas and shifts influencing the future of business and society.

The final programme adds Felix Cheung, founder and CEO of the Bairong Group in China; Kim Hulett, biotech entrepreneur and founder of Next Biosciences; Shayne Mann, co-CEO of Singularity South Africa and CEO of Mann Made; Ran Neuner, founder of Crypto Banter; Hywel George, global investor and former chief investment officer; Marko Stavrou, creator economy specialist; and Rajesh Pasungili, founder and CEO of Resolute Education, to an already extensive line-up of global and African innovators, entrepreneurs, business leaders and technology specialists.

They join previously announced speakers including AI specialists Amanda Manna and Dario Fanucchi, robotics pioneer Tilly Lockey, enterprise AI leader Barak Kaufman, digital transformation expert Valter Adão, Hamed Kazim, and South African inventor Fana Shabane. Acclaimed poet, author and broadcaster Lebo Mashile will return as the Summit’s poet and MC.

From AI to the future of business

Artificial intelligence will be one of the major themes of the two-day programme, with speakers examining its rapid evolution, the challenge of moving enterprise AI from experimentation to implementation and what the next generation of AI could mean for organisations and their people.

The conversation will extend into digital transformation, leadership, entrepreneurship, investment, robotics, the future of cities and the changing skills required to navigate an increasingly technology-driven economy.

“The conversation around technology has shifted significantly. Business leaders are no longer asking whether AI and other exponential technologies will affect their organisations, but where to invest, how to implement them effectively and how to prepare their people for the changes ahead,” says Mic Mann, co-CEO of Singularity South Africa.

“The Summit creates an opportunity to step outside the day-to-day demands of running an organisation and engage with the bigger shifts taking place. The aim is for delegates to leave better informed, better connected and with a clearer sense of where the opportunities lie,” added Shayne Mann, co-CEO of Singularity South Africa.

Celiwe Ross, group chief human capital and corporate affairs officer at Old Mutual says the future will not be defined by technology alone, but by how people choose to use it. “I would encourage business leaders, investors and professionals from across industries to be part of this conversation, because the future is not only about the technologies we adopt, but about how we equip our people to grow, respond and lead in an environment that is constantly changing.

"As AI and other exponential technologies accelerate the pace of disruption, leaders have an opportunity to think differently about how technology can unlock human potential, create new opportunities and shape more inclusive growth. The organisations that thrive will be those that prepare their people and their cultures for change, rather than simply preparing for the next technology. The Summit brings together some of the world’s leading thinkers, innovators and entrepreneurs to explore these shifts and, importantly, what they mean for people, business and Africa’s future,” Ross says.

Global perspectives with an African lens

While the programme brings international expertise to Johannesburg, the Summit will also examine these developments through an African lens, including how businesses on the continent can harness new technologies, where new opportunities for innovation and investment are emerging and how African entrepreneurs and innovators can play a greater role in shaping the global technology landscape.

Alongside keynote presentations, the programme will feature panel discussions bringing together different perspectives on some of the most pressing questions facing business leaders. Delegates will also have access to various AI workshops and masterclasses to upskill and empower our community. An interactive expo showcasing emerging technologies and innovations, as well as networking opportunities with speakers, executives, entrepreneurs and fellow delegates.

The announcement of the full programme marks the final stage in the build-up to Singularity Summit South Africa 2026, with more than 40 speakers contributing to two days of keynote presentations, discussions, panels, interactive experiences and networking.

For more information, regular updates or to book, visit www.singularitysouthafricaSummit.org.

data.title: Syngenta files for Hong Kong IPO, aiming to raise at least $5 billion, sources say
data.description:
Swiss seeds and agrichemicals company Syngenta Group has confidentially filed for a Hong Kong initial public offering, aiming to raise at least $5 billion, according to two people with direct knowledge of the matter.

The Basel-based company, controlled by Chinese state-owned Sinochem , hopes to launch the offering as soon as the end of this year, or if not early 2027, said one of the sources.

Depending on the market response, the offering size could be up to $10 billion, the sources said. At that size, it would be Hong Kong's biggest IPO since 2010, according to LSEG data.

The exact timing, offering size and the company's valuation have not been finalised, said the sources, who declined to be named as the information was not public.

"We do not comment on market speculation," Syngenta said in

a response to Reuters. Sinochem did not immediately respond to a

request for comment.

Bloomberg News first reported on the filing on Tuesday, saying the company is considering raising about $5 billion.

data.title: OTB's Jil Sander appoints former Moncler executive Marco Viganò as new CEO
data.description:
Fashion brand Jil Sander, owned by Italy's luxury group OTB, appointed Marco Viganò as new Chief Executive, effective September 15, the company said on Tuesday.

  • Viganò will report to the Group CEO Ubaldo Minelli, who has led the brand on an interim basis since Serge Brunschwig stepped down in July 2025, after six months in the role.

  • "Marco's experience and knowledge of international markets will contribute to the brand's growth journey, supporting its development and further strengthening its positioning," Minelli said in the statement.

  • Viganò joins Jil Sander from luxury outerwear group Moncler , where he served as Global Chief Client Officer and President for EMEA.

  • Previously, he was Chief Commercial Officer at Swiss watchmaker Audemars Piguet and Chief Operating Officer at Saint Laurent. He has also held roles at Louis Vuitton , Kering's Gucci and L'Oréal .

data.description: MJ Gleeson faces a challenging trading backdrop but sees adjusted pretax profit for fiscal 2027 in line with views. Peel Hunt analysts Sam Cullen and Clyde Lewis say the home builder will operate from slightly fewer sites as build-cost inflation remains a headwind for the entire industry. Excessive regulatory and tax burdens are also a factor. "We remain constructive on the group, and continue to believe it is well-placed to deliver growth when the market allows," Peel Hunt says. data.title: Stocks enter the 'Danger Zone'
data.description:
Key points:
  • STOXX 600 down 0.7%, 3-month low
  • Oil prices rise over 2%
  • Dollar, global bond yields up
  • Wall Street futures drop

STOCKS ENTER THE "DANGER ZONE"

Investors are making their way through September with plenty to worry about, from higher oil prices to expectations of further interest-rate increases in the United States and Japan.

According to research firm SentimenTrader, market internals are also flashing an increasingly cautionary signal.

Its Market Environment Composite (MEC), which tracks eight indicators of market breadth and behaviour, stands at 2.

That places it in what it calls the "Danger Zone", a level historically associated with weak returns and elevated risk: "The market environment has fallen into an unhealthy state."

MEC readings of 2 to 4 points have historically produced annualised losses of 6% to 10% for the S&P 500, whereas readings of 5 to 7 were associated with annualised gains of 11% to 13%.

At the extremes of the spectrum, 0 or 1 signal extreme panic and have historically offered strong opportunities, with returns of more than 30%, while a reading of 8 points to an overheated market and often coincided with market tops.

SentimenTrader says the indicator is not intended as a market-timing tool, but can help investors avoid staying on the wrong side of the market for too long.

"Aggressive traders can monitor the MEC for a drop into extreme panic territory to hunt for bottom-fishing opportunities, but this must be paired with strict stop-loss strategies."
